newsitem.title: USA: AOL makes Excite exclusive directory.
newsitem.headline: AOL makes Excite exclusive directory.

text.p: America Online will make Excite Inc. the exclusive Internet search and directory service for America Online's more than 7 million subscribers under a deal announced by the two companies Monday.

Excite will also acquire Dulles, Va.-based America Online's WebCrawler search and directory service for about 2 million shares of Excite, raising AOL's ownership of Excite to about 20 percent from its current 10 percent, the companies said.
Excite stock rocketed $3.75 to $9.875, making it one of top 10 percentage gainers on Nasdaq. America Online rose $1.625 to $32.625 on the New York Stock Exchange.

The companies said they will explore ways to better integrate "smart search" capabilities throughout America Online, the world's No. 1 online service. These capabilities will allow AOL subscribers to search through the service's content more swiftly and efficiently, a spokesman said.
AOL and Excite said the deal will enable them to create a powerful medium for advertisers and merchants, producing additional advertising revenues for both companies.
Under the deal, AOL has been granted a seat on Excite's board, which will be filled by AOL Chairman Steve Case.
Bob Pittman, who was an independent director on Excite's board before joining AOL as president of its AOL Networks unit, has resigned from the board.
The WebCrawler purchase is expected to be completed in early 1997.
